steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper SemSegDepth, a multi-task network that does semantic segmentation and depth completion together. Motivate multi-task scene understanding, define the two tasks and why combining them is hard, and give an overview of our architecture and evaluation.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Holistic scene understanding: humans vs machines
- Multi-task networks and the semantic segmentation + depth completion combination
- Definitions of the two tasks and why combining them helps
- Our model SemSegDepth: architecture and evaluation

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Holistic scene understanding
  - computer vision / holistic scene understanding pivotal for autonomous machines
  - humans: unconsciously assign multiple attributes, multiple tasks at once (distance, quantity, size, texture...); understand semantic complexity
  - machines outperform humans on single tasks: object detection, semantic segmentation, depth estimation
  - multiple tasks: machines still lag behind humans
- Multi-task networks
  - highly active field; more complete scene representation
  - growing evidence multi-task improves each individual task
  - e.g. panoptic segmentation: instance segmentation + object detection + semantic segmentation
  - only few methods combine semantic segmentation + depth completion
  - extra challenge vs panoptic: heterogeneous data jointly (RGB for segmentation, sparse depth for completion)
- Task definitions
  - semantic segmentation: semantic label per pixel ("car", "person", "bike", "background")
  - depth completion: distance of every pixel, usually sparse depth input
  - autonomous driving: combination improves whole system; semantic understanding + proximity of things
- SemSegDepth
  - new end-to-end multi-task network, semantic segmentation + depth completion jointly
  - combines two benchmarking models: modified depth completion network from prior work + modified EfficientPS
  - overview in Figure 1: feature extractor, semantic segmentation branch, depth completion branch, joint branch
  - feature extractor: resnet50 in Feature Pyramid Network (FPN)
  - segmentation branch based on EfficientPS's; depth branch adds semantic logits as input; joint branch processes semantic + depth together
  - trained/evaluated on Virtual KITTI 2; improves both tasks

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Computer vision and holistic scene understanding have become very important topics as we try to give machines autonomous capabilities. When we as humans see things, we unconsciously assign multiple attributes to what we see, and we also do multiple tasks at the same time. For example, we can assess the distance of the objects we see, the quantity, the size, the texture, etc. all at once. We can also understand the world around us in its semantic complexity. Machines, on the other hand, can outperform humans in several tasks individually. This is the case for object detection, semantic segmentation and/or depth estimation, where machines have successfully carried out these tasks individually. But when it comes to doing multiple tasks, machines are still behind humans.

Multi-task networks have become a very active field of research in computer vision, as an attempt to give a more holistic approach to scene understanding. Besides giving a more complete representation of a scene, there is growing evidence that multi-task networks can improve the performance of each individual task. For example, panoptic segmentation combines instance segmentation, object detection and semantic segmentation. As far as we know, only few methods have combined semantic segmentation and depth completion. Compared to other applications like panoptic segmentation, combining semantic segmentation and depth completion has additional challenges, like processing heterogeneous data jointly, because semantic segmentation relies on RGB images and depth completion relies on sparse depth data.

- semantic segmentation: semantic label per pixel ("car", "person", "bike", "background")
- depth completion: distance of every pixel, usually sparse depth input given
- autonomous driving: combining both improves the whole system (semantic understanding + proximity of things)
- our model: new end-to-end multi-task network; modified depth completion network from earlier work + modified EfficientPS
- Figure 1: feature extractor (resnet50 in FPN), semantic segmentation branch (from EfficientPS), depth completion branch (adds semantic logits as input), joint branch
- trained/evaluated on Virtual KITTI 2; improves both tasks

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Computer vision and holistic scene understanding have become very important topics as we try to give machines autonomous capabilities. When we as humans see things, we unconsciously assign multiple attributes to what we see, and we also do multiple tasks at the same time. For example, we can assess the distance of the objects we see, the quantity, the size, the texture, etc. all at once. We can also understand the world around us in its semantic complexity. Machines, on the other hand, can outperform humans in several tasks individually. This is the case for object detection, semantic segmentation and/or depth estimation, where machines have successfully carried out these tasks individually. But when it comes to doing multiple tasks, machines are still behind humans.

Multi-task networks have become a very active field of research in computer vision, as an attempt to give a more holistic approach to scene understanding. Besides giving a more complete representation of a scene, there is growing evidence that multi-task networks can improve the performance of each individual task. For example, panoptic segmentation combines instance segmentation, object detection and semantic segmentation. As far as we know, only few methods have combined semantic segmentation and depth completion. Compared to other applications like panoptic segmentation, combining semantic segmentation and depth completion has additional challenges, like processing heterogeneous data jointly, because semantic segmentation relies on RGB images and depth completion relies on sparse depth data.

Semantic segmentation is the task of assigning a semantic label to every pixel in an image, for example deciding whether a pixel belongs to a "car", "person", "bike" or "background". Depth estimation, and more specifically depth completion, predicts the distance of every pixel in an image, where in most cases a sparse depth input is given. In applications like autonomous driving, combining semantic segmentation and depth completion can significantly improve the performance of the system as a whole, since the machines would understand their surroundings semantically and they would also know about the proximity of the things in a given scenario.

In this paper we propose a new end-to-end multi-task network that does semantic segmentation and depth completion jointly. We combine two benchmarking models: a modified version of the depth completion network proposed in earlier work and a modified version of EfficientPS. Figure 1 shows an overview of our model SemSegDepth. It has a feature extractor, a semantic segmentation branch, a depth completion branch and a joint branch. The feature extractor is a resnet50 network wrapped in a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN). Our semantic segmentation branch is based on the semantic segmentation branch of the EfficientPS architecture. The depth completion branch extends that earlier network by adding semantic logits as input, and the joint branch processes the semantic and depth information further together. We trained and evaluated our model on Virtual KITTI 2 and showed that SemSegDepth improves the performance of both tasks, semantic segmentation and depth completion.

In this paper we propose a new end-to-end multi-task network that does semantic segmentation and depth completion jointly. We combine two benchmarking models: a modified version of the depth completion network proposed in earlier work [7] and a modified version of EfficientPS [11]. steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Computer vision and holistic scene understanding have become pivotal topics as we intend to give machines autonomous capabilities. When we, as humans, see things, we unconsciously assign multiple attributes to what we see, and we also perform multiple tasks simultaneously. For instance, we can effectively assess the distance of the objects we see, their quantity, size, texture, etc. all at once, and we are capable of understanding the world around us in its semantic complexity. Machines, on the other hand, can outperform humans in several tasks individually, as is the case for object detection [1], [2], [3], semantic segmentation [4], [5], [6] and/or depth estimation [7], [8], [9]. However, when it comes to performing multiple tasks, machines are still lagging behind humans.

In an attempt to provide a more holistic approach to scene understanding, multi-task networks have become a highly active field of research in computer vision. In addition to providing a more complete representation of a scene, there is growing evidence that multi-task networks can improve the performance of each individual task [10]. Panoptic segmentation, for example, combines instance segmentation, object detection and semantic segmentation [11], [12], [13], [14]. To our best knowledge, only few methods have combined semantic segmentation and depth completion [15], [16]. Compared to other applications such as panoptic segmentation, combining semantic segmentation and depth completion poses additional challenges, such as processing heterogeneous data jointly, since semantic segmentation relies on RGB images while depth completion relies on sparse depth data.

Semantic segmentation refers to the task of assigning a semantic label to every single pixel in an image, e.g. determining whether a pixel belongs to a "car", "person", "bike" or "background". Depth estimation, more specifically depth completion, predicts the distance of every pixel in an image, where in most cases a sparse depth input is provided. In applications such as autonomous driving, combining semantic segmentation and depth completion can significantly improve the performance of the system as a whole, as the machines would not only understand their surroundings semantically but would also have knowledge about the proximity of things in a given scenario.

In this paper we propose a new end-to-end multi-task network for performing semantic segmentation and depth completion jointly. We combine two benchmarking models, using a modified version of the depth completion network proposed by [7] and a modified version of EfficientPS [11]. An overview of our model SemSegDepth is shown in Figure 1. It consists of a feature extractor, a semantic segmentation branch, a depth completion branch and a joint branch. The feature extractor is a resnet50 network [17] wrapped in a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) [18]. Our semantic segmentation branch is based on that of the EfficientPS architecture, the depth completion branch extends [7] by adding semantic logits as input, and the joint branch further processes semantic and depth information together. We trained and evaluated our model on Virtual KITTI 2 [19] and demonstrated that SemSegDepth improves the performance of both tasks, semantic segmentation and depth completion.
